raw_segments.text: In the present season of scarcity, the high price of corn no doubt distresses the poor.
But in times of moderate plenty, when corn is at its ordinary or average price, the natural
rise in the price of any other sort of rude produce cannot much affect them.
They suffer more, perhaps, by the artificial rise which has been occasioned by taxes and
the price of some manufactured commodities, as of salt, soap, leather, candles, malt,
